A titanic ancestral fortress erupts from a black crag — five mismatched towers of wildly unequal height bristling with arrow-slits and finials, linked by crenellated curtain-walls and a pair of arched stone skywalks that leap between battlements. The great central keep hunches behind a bristling forest of lesser turrets, its facade riddled with lancet windows glowing amber deep within the stone.

A grand Victorian haunted mansion sprawls across a dead lawn — asymmetric wings lurching at odd angles, a wraparound porch sagging at the corners, three conical turrets of different heights clustered at the facade, broken shutters hanging half-open, and a widow's-walk railing twisted like arthritic fingers above the topmost gable. Every dormer is cracked, every chimney stack leaning.

A ruined gothic abbey-castle swallowed in centuries of ivy — the vast nave open to the heavens through a collapsed ribbed vault, flying buttresses still arching gracefully over emptiness, a half-standing chapter-house tower draped in creeper, crumbling tracery rose-windows framing darkness, and a collapsed transept wall leaning dramatically against a thicket of stone pinnacles still stubbornly intact.

A fairytale-gone-dark fantasy castle of impossible asymmetry — clusters of needle-thin obsidian spires of wildly different heights, a cantilevered gallery jutting over a sheer drop on iron brackets, stepped cascade rooflines tumbling down the hillside in dark slate tiers, and a great bridge of stone sweeping from the gatehouse to a detached tower standing alone across a chasm.

A gothic sea-fortress clinging to jagged coastal cliffs — massive ramparts of salt-eaten black granite stepping down the rock face in three terraced tiers, squat drum towers at each corner punched with cross-loop windows, a great sea-gate arch battered by spray below, and an upper citadel with four uneven spires leaning slightly inward as if bracing against perpetual Atlantic wind.

A sprawling manor-estate of decayed Crimson-Peak grandeur — a wide asymmetric facade of crumbling terracotta and blackened stone, six ornate chimneys of twisted brick rising at uneven intervals, a long colonnaded wing sinking visibly at one end, broken conservatory glasswork framing dead vines, and a central entrance tower with a stepped gable and a clock-face frozen at midnight.

A crooked witch's tower-house leaning precipitously over a cobbled lane — three stacked timber-framed stories of wildly mismatched width, each floor jutting further than the last in precarious corbelled overhangs, a spiraling conical cap tilted at an alarming angle, candlelit lancet windows of thick green glass, and exterior staircases of wrought iron spiraling up the outside like dark vines.

A gothic cathedral-clocktower hybrid of astonishing vertical complexity — a massive clock-face of verdigris bronze set into a soaring belltower flanked by two smaller spire-capped towers, the whole facade encrusted with gargoyle balustrades at every cornice level, flying buttresses sweeping outward from the nave, and a great rose window cracked down the center, its tracery still intact and exquisite.

A decaying Southern plantation-gothic mansion deep in overgrown grounds — a broad colonnaded double-gallery facade draped in cascading spanish moss and strangling wisteria, wings sprawling left and right beyond the columns, a central roof cupola with broken jalousies, two flanking octagonal pavilions connected by crumbling covered walkways, and a grand exterior double-staircase whose wrought-iron railing is half-consumed by creeping vine.

A palace of black obsidian gothic spires rising from frozen ground — faceted dark stone walls that catch and fracture light into cold shards, a forest of needle spires of dramatically unequal height clustered in three groups linked by arched glass-and-iron skywalks, a broad rampart terrace with iron balustrades, and a gatehouse of two massive flanking towers whose archway is sealed with a portcullis of gleaming black iron.

A castle of stacked tiers and buttressed terraces climbing a sheer crag — five distinct levels of ramparts each set back from the one below, connected by exterior stone staircases and fortified galleries, a great keep at the summit bristling with four corner turrets, massive flying buttresses arching from the third terrace outward into nothing, and lower walls studded with blind arcading and narrow slit windows.

A Addams-Family-energy Victorian haunted house of spectacular lopsided sprawl — a central three-story mansard body flanked by a tall octagonal tower on the left and a wide gabled wing on the right, a wraparound porch with elaborate spindle-work fretwork rotting at the joints, two dormers on each roof slope with broken stained glass, and a rooftop widow's-walk surrounded by a cast-iron railing in the shape of intertwined thorns.

A ruined gothic fortress-cathedral at the edge of a forest — the skeletal ribbed vault of the nave still spanning overhead despite the collapsed clerestory walls, a pair of western towers standing intact with their spires, a cloister of slender colonettes half-standing to the south, the chapter house tower draped in moss but intact, and great carved portal tympana still legible in limestone despite centuries of weather.

A fairytale-gothic castle of Howl's-Moving-Castle complexity — wings and sub-towers added in wildly different eras jostling at odd angles, a great round tower with a stepped conical roof dominating the right, a glass-and-iron conservatory ballooning from the left wing, exterior iron staircases zigzagging between levels, and a drawbridge opening onto a stone-arched covered passage that tunnels through a lower bastion before emerging at the gatehouse.

A cliffside gothic stronghold of Bloodborne-cathedral-city verticality — towers and rampart-walkways stacked at five different elevations connected by exterior stone staircases and iron-railed galleries cantilevered over the drop, the lowest wall vanishing into sea-spray at the base of the cliff, gargoyle waterspouts jutting from every parapet, and the highest tower tilted very slightly outward over the void as if straining toward the open water below.

A grand haunted manor in full Hill-House sprawl — an immense asymmetric pile of dark Victorian Gothic with gabled wings extending in three directions, clusters of decorative chimneys in barley-twist brick, a great porte-cochère with pointed arches and carved foliate capitals, broken lancet windows fitted with iron grilles, and at the far end a round tower rising two stories above the roofline with a corbelled parapet walk.

A frost palace of gothic impossible geometry — slender towers of pale blue-veined stone rising in groups of three and five, each capped with a needle finial of what appears to be spun ice, the facade a lattice of pointed arches within arches, broad terrace walkways with crystal-clear balustrades etched in delicate tracery, and a vast ceremonial stair of thirty steps descending from the great arched portal to a frozen forecourt.

A ruined gothic abbey swallowed by forest — the skeletal arcade of the cloister walkway still intact and traced in climbing ivy, the great tower at the crossing half-collapsed to a dramatic jagged crown, three remaining walls of the nave covered in centuries of moss and lichen with their blind arcading still legible, and a chapter house entrance portal with carved voussoirs intact, its tympanum sculpture worn to ghostly smoothness.

A Tim-Burton-energy witch's tower-house of spectacular crookedness — four stacked stories of increasing width, each floor overhanging the last on exaggerated corbels, the whole structure leaning fifteen degrees to the left, a roofline of multiple overlapping pointed gables of different scales, exterior pipework and iron conduits snaking up the walls, and every window of a different shape — round, lancet, diamond, hexagonal — each glowing a different dim color from within.

A Southern Gothic plantation mansion consumed by time and vine — a once-grand double-gallery colonnade of tall round columns, several now cracked and bound with iron repair-collars, flanking wings of different heights and eras connected by covered breezeways, an octagonal belvedere above the main roof with broken jalousie shutters, and the entire facade half-engulfed in a living curtain of spanish moss, wisteria, and tangling moonflower vine.

A gothic clocktower-cathedral of Castlevania grandeur — a soaring main belltower flanked by two narrower spire-towers, the clock-face enormous and worked in verdigris bronze with ornate Gothic numerals, the lower facade an encyclopedia of carved gargoyles and grotesques at every corbel and capital, great flying buttresses sweeping to flanking stair-turrets, and the portal arch deeply recessed behind five concentric orders of carved stone.

A dark obsidian fairytale-gothic palace of Minas-Morgul drama — walls of gleaming black stone carved from a single mountain face, a great stepped facade ascending in three dramatic setbacks each edged with pointed merlons, four flanking towers of wildly different profiles — round, square, hexagonal, and polygonal — connected by glass-roofed iron skywalks at the third level, and a vast ceremonial gate of worked iron shaped into interlocking thorn-arch forms.

A multi-spire ancestral castle fortress of jaw-dropping silhouette — a great curtain wall enclosing a courtyard dominated by a central keep with four corner bartizans, the whole ringed by an outer ward with six mural towers of slightly different heights and profiles, a double-towered gatehouse of massive scale, exterior stair-towers climbing the curtain wall faces, and the entire skyline bristling with finials, merlons, and corbelled parapet walkways at three different heights.

A grand crumbling Victorian haunted manor of Allerdale-Hall scale — a wide rusting wrought-iron gate opening onto a facade of dark red brick gone almost black with damp, a central entrance tower with a stepped Flemish gable and a rusted weathervane, two sprawling wings of wildly different character — one Tudor-revival, one Italianate — each with their own cluster of chimneys and gabled dormers, and a long conservatory of broken glass along the south elevation.

A sea-cliff gothic stronghold of spectacular cascading complexity — the fortress descending the cliff face in five terraced rampart levels each wider than the one above, the lowest terrace a sea-wall arch through which waves surge, drum towers at every terrace corner with corbelled parapet walks, the highest citadel with three mismatched spires and a great hall window of blind tracery, and an exterior stone staircase zig-zagging down the cliff face between all five levels.

[A] A colossal ancestral fortress crowns a sheer basalt crag, its central keep flanked by six curtain-wall towers of staggered heights, connected by stone walkways arching over nothing. Battlements step downward in dramatic cascading tiers, each level bristling with spear-thin pinnacles. Iron portcullis chains hang slack, gargoyles lean outward from every parapet corner, and the whole sprawling silhouette claws across the ridge like a stone behemoth.

[B] A grand Victorian haunted mansion stretches wide across a dead lawn — three asymmetrical turrets of unequal height anchoring each wing, a wraparound porch sagging at one end with broken spindles dangling loose. Dozens of gabled dormers crowd the roofline at wild angles, a widow's walk tilts slightly off-true, and every tall shuttered window shows one pane cracked inward, the lace behind it stirring without wind.

[J] A palace of pure obsidian rises in impossible gothic tiers, its clustered spires faceted like black crystal and refracting cold light in dark rainbow shards. Pointed arches stack upon pointed arches in repeating geometric excess, flying buttresses curve like recurved blades between towers, and a vast central facade is carved floor-to-parapet with intertwining thorned vines cast entirely in gleaming black stone.

[D] A fairytale-gothic fantasy castle explodes upward in glorious asymmetry — one tower wide and squat with a flared mushroom-cap roof, another needle-thin and leaning slightly left, a third wrapped in spiraling exterior staircases that connect to a cantilevered bridge suspended over open air. Candy-thin turrets cluster in groups of five, their conical roofs painted the deep blue of old bruises, every surface crammed with carved tracery.

[E] A gothic sea-fortress clings to a jagged coastal stack, its lowest walls slick and barnacle-eaten where waves have eaten the stone for centuries. Four massive towers of different ages and stone colors are lashed together by later-built arched skywalks, the oldest tower already half-crumbled to a dramatic ruin. Iron chains thick as a man's torso run from the gatehouse down into the churning water below.

A colossal ancestral fortress erupts from a black crag — five mismatched towers of wildly different heights bristling with iron finials, curtain-walls bristling with crenellations, a great central keep flanked by drum towers, flying bridges arching between battlements, every surface carved with gargoyles and blind arcading, the whole silhouette jagged and asymmetrical and absolutely breathtaking against the open sky.

A grand Victorian haunted mansion sprawls across a dead hillside — wraparound porch sagging under ornate fretwork, a widow's walk crowning the central gable, turrets at every corner with broken fish-scale shingles, dormers erupting at odd angles, shutters hanging loose, the facade a gorgeous wreck of spindle-work and peeling gingerbread trim glowing faintly from within.

A ruined gothic abbey-castle swallowed by centuries of ivy — the great rose window still intact above a collapsed nave, flying buttresses marching along the flank like stone ribs, a half-standing bell tower leaning gently, crumbling choir walls open to the sky, the whole ruin enormous and glorious rather than mere rubble, arches framing arches framing darkness.

A fairytale-gothic fantasy castle of impossible geometry — clusters of needle-thin spires of wildly different heights spiral upward like frozen black flames, cantilevered wings jut over nothing, a great arched skywalk connects two erupting tower-clusters, tiers of buttressed terraces step down the cliff-face, the whole structure asymmetrical and dreamlike and absolutely wild.

A gothic sea-fortress claws the face of a jagged coastal cliff — ramparts grown directly from the rock, wave-battered curtain-walls dropping sheer to churning water below, three massive towers staggered at different heights along the clifftop, iron sea-gates trailing rusted chains, every stone stained dark by salt and age, the silhouette ragged and dramatic.

A sprawling gothic manor-estate sags gloriously across a marshy plain — Allerdale-Hall grandeur, ornate clustered chimneys erupting from every roofline, stepped gables cascading across the facade, a long colonnaded entrance flanked by crumbling outbuildings, the whole central block listing slightly to one side as if slowly returning to the earth, breathtaking in its decayed magnificence.

A crooked witch's tower-house leans at an impossible angle — four stacked stories of spindly gothic stonework, each floor slightly offset from the last, lancet windows glowing amber, a tiny turret erupting sideways from the third level, iron weather-vanes at every peak, the whole structure draped in dead wisteria and looking as though it grew rather than was built.

A gothic clocktower-cathedral hybrid dominates a ridge — the enormous clock-face set into a vast decorated gable flanked by twin bell-towers, gargoyle balustrades ringing every tier, flying buttresses springing from the flanks, a forest of pinnacles crowning the roofline, the whole facade elaborately carved with blind tracery and niched saints worn smooth, soaring and theatrical and spine-tingling.

A southern plantation-gothic mansion crumbles magnificently behind a colonnade of tilting pillars wound in spanish moss and strangler vine — the colonnaded facade stretching wide and low, upper balconies sagging with ornate ironwork railings, dormer windows broken and dark, great chimneys listing at odd angles, the whole estate swallowed in greenery yet still commanding, still haunted, still grand.

A frost palace of obsidian gothic spires rises from a frozen plateau — black glass-stone carved into cathedral tracery, impossibly thin spires clustering at varying heights and glittering darkly, arched bridges spanning between tower clusters, elaborate pinnacles and crockets of what appears to be frozen shadow, every surface faceted and gleaming, the silhouette jagged and magnificent and utterly unearthly.

A Castlevania-scale ancestral castle crowns a mountain's shattered summit — a great central keep ringed by a forest of smaller towers of every height, curtain-walls stepping down the crag in terraced rings, arched skywalks connecting every tier, the whole fortress spreading wide across the ridgeline rather than climbing upward, a silhouette of layered horizontal complexity and absolute gothic grandeur.

A haunted Victorian seaside manor perches on eroding chalk bluffs — the wraparound porch winds three sides of the building and sags at the seaward corner, turrets of mismatched diameter rise at each wing, fish-scale shingles cover the upper stories in alternating bands of decay, a widow's walk bristling with broken finials crowns the tallest gable, the whole house spectacular and doomed.

A ruined cathedral-fortress of red sandstone erupts from a wooded valley floor — the crossing tower still standing tall and elaborate above a roofless nave open to the sky, chapels and transepts in various states of magnificent collapse, stone choir stalls visible through broken tracery windows, the west front still complete with its tympanum and colonettes, ivy threading every joint with green fire.

A dark fairytale castle of layered impossibility spreads across a misty plateau — seven towers of drastically different profiles cluster together, round and square and hexagonal and octagonal, connected by a mad tangle of arched bridges and stepped flying walkways, every roofline at a different pitch, the overall silhouette wide and sprawling and thrillingly complex, like a city compressed into a single structure.

A gothic cliff-castle grafted directly onto a sea-stack — the natural pillar of rock capped by rings of curtain-wall and then a keep and then towers erupting from the keep, connected to the clifftop by a single narrow arched bridge of breathtaking span, the whole structure reflected in the churning water below, remote and theatrical and impossibly dramatic against the open sky.

A decayed gothic manor-estate of immense horizontal sprawl — flanking wings stretching far on each side of the central block, each wing crowned with a different roofline profile, clustered ornate chimneys at every interval, grand stone staircases sweeping down from the entrance terrace, the whole facade ornamented with pilasters and blind arches and stone urns cracked by frost, majestic in its ruin.

A storybook witch's tower-cluster of spindly leaning gothic masonry — not one tower but five, all different heights and girth, fused together at odd angles and connected by tiny arched bridges, each topped with a different kind of finial, amber windows scattered irregularly across every face, the whole impossible agglomeration wrapped in dead ivy and leaning gently into each other like conspirators.

A gothic clocktower of staggering height and elaboration — the great four-faced clock set into a carved stone drum above the main belfry, flanked by slender turrets with copper-green spirelets, the lower stages wrapped in blind Gothic arcading and gargoyle water-spouts, a grand processional stair sweeping up to the main door, the whole structure wide-based and horizontally rich before it soars.

A southern gothic plantation house of extraordinary and ruinous grandeur — two symmetrical wings sprawl from a pedimented centre, the colonnade of twelve massive pillars trailing spanish moss to the ground, ironwork balconies on the upper floor twisted and green, every window broken or shuttered, the formal garden in front reduced to stone balustrades swallowed by dark flowering vine, hauntingly beautiful.

An obsidian gothic palace encrusted with black-crystal pinnacles — the main facade a cliff of dark carved stone pierced by enormous lancet windows backed with what appears to be frozen amber light, flanking towers of different diameters rising to elaborate openwork crowns, a grand arched gate flanked by paired buttress-piers carved into the shapes of vast hooded figures, glittering and forbidding and jaw-dropping.

A Bloodborne-cathedral-city gothic fortress stacks tier upon tier up a sheer escarpment — each level a new ring of curtain-walls and towers, connected by exterior staircases and arched bridges, the uppermost keep bristling with clustered spires of different heights, the lowest level of blind arches half-buried in the cliff, the overall silhouette a wedding-cake of gothic verticals spreading wide across the frame.

A Victorian haunted mansion of extreme asymmetry commands a dead garden — the left wing two full stories taller than the right, a round turret on one corner answered by a polygonal bay on the other, a sweeping porte-cochère arching across the front drive, dormers of different shapes erupting from the roofline at irregular intervals, the wraparound porch sagging in the middle, gorgeously unhinged.

A ruined gothic abbey of cathedral scale rises from a tidal island — the great west front standing nearly complete with its three portals and enormous wheel window, the nave walls roofless and ivy-covered yet still soaring, the chapter-house intact with its palm-vault visible through a broken wall, the whole ruin connected by a narrow causeway of cracked stone to the shore, magnificent and melancholy.

A dark fantasy castle of insane silhouette complexity spreads across twin crags connected by a natural arch — each crag crowned by its own tower-cluster, the arch below spanned by a great hall with enormous gothic windows, additional towers erupting from the arch itself, flying bridges connecting every element at every height, the combined silhouette wider than tall and absolutely wild, a fever-dream of gothic ambition.

A frost-glass gothic palace of mirror-dark spires reflects its own impossible geometry — the central facade a wall of black faceted stone carved into cathedral tracery and flanked by four towers of different heights all topped with openwork crowns of spun obsidian, grand exterior staircases of glittering black stone sweeping to a monumental gate, the whole structure spreading low and wide and breathtakingly alien.

A titanic ancestral fortress crowns a sheer basalt crag, its curtain-walls sweeping left and right like stone arms, bristling with a dozen mismatched towers — squat drum-keeps, needle spires, and fat round bastions clustered at wildly different heights. Flying bridges arc between them. The great central keep rises in stacked tiers of black granite, every parapet crenellated and corbelled, gargoyles jutting from each corner. [A]

A grand Victorian mansion sprawls across a dead estate, its wraparound porch sagging but still imperious, three asymmetrical turrets crowned with witch-hat roofs rising at opposing corners. Broken shutters hang at angles. A widow's-walk rails the topmost gable, its ironwork twisted like thorns. Bay windows bulge from the facade. Every roofline stacks a new gabled peak behind the last, creating a silhouette of cascading dark teeth. [B]

A ruined gothic abbey-castle consumes an entire hilltop, its cathedral nave open to the elements, the collapsed roof replaced by a lattice of bare stone ribs and creeping ivy. Twin bell-towers still stand, cracked and leaning toward each other. Flying buttresses arc between them, half-choked in vines. Massive pointed windows, their tracery intact, frame pure darkness within. Crumbling chapter-house wings flank the nave in decayed splendor. [C]

A fairytale castle of impossible, deranged beauty stretches across a ridge, its spires of wildly different widths and heights clustering like an argument — some corkscrew, some faceted like dark crystals, some flared at the top like inverted bells. Covered bridges and arched skywalks connect them at dizzying heights. Every surface is carved in gothic tracery. The whole composition leans slightly leftward, dreamily, as though the castle is listening. [D]

A gothic sea-fortress clings to a finger of jagged coastal rock, its base walls drenched by spray, black with salt and age. The castle climbs in three distinct tiers — a sea-gate with a portcullis, a mid-fortress of pointed arches and cannon-slits, and a high keep ringed by four towers with iron-capped spires. Crumbling battlements at each level create a dramatic stepped silhouette against open sky. [E]

Allerdale-Hall-like gothic manor sprawls across a sinking moor, its vast facade dominated by twelve ornate chimney-stacks of twisted brick rising like fingers. Symmetrical wings extend far left and right, each terminating in a pedimented gable. The central entrance portico drips with carved stone foliage. Sagging bay windows line both wings. The entire structure lists almost imperceptibly to one side, its foundations slowly surrendering to the dark earth below. [F]

A spindly crooked tower-cottage of impossible height leans hard to the right, its stacked floors each offset from the one below, giving the whole structure a spiraling organic silhouette. Gothic lancet windows glow amber at every story. A steep crow-stepped gable crowns the peak. Wrought-iron finials bristle from every corner. A lower attached cottage wing, itself lopsided, extends to one side, its chimney crooked as a broken finger. [G]

A cathedral-clocktower hybrid dominates its hill, an enormous clock-face of blackened iron and cracked enamel set into the base of the belltower, flanked by gargoyle balustrades snarling outward. Above it the tower splits into three ascending stages of gothic arcading, each ringed with flying buttresses. Lateral nave-wings extend wide to either side, their rose-windows dark and fractured. The whole structure is ornate, severe, and overwhelmingly vertical in all directions. [H]

A decaying Southern plantation-gothic mansion commands a long oak alley, its white colonnaded facade now gray and veined with creeping vine, spanish moss draped from every horizontal surface like mourning cloth. Twin flanking dependencies connect to the main house by low covered walkways with pointed gothic arches. Above the cornice a second story of pointed dormers erupts, then a widow's-walk, then an octagonal belvedere gone black with age. [I]

A palace of pure obsidian rises in a forest of thin impossibly-tall spires, every surface faceted to catch and shatter light into dark rainbows. The main body is a wide horizontal keep of jet-black stone carved with gothic tracery so fine it reads as lace. Buttresses of the same black stone arc outward at dramatic angles. The silhouette is wide and low at center, erupting vertically at both flanks in a crown of needle-spires. [J]

A multi-winged ancestral castle spreads across a mountain shoulder in four distinct building campaigns, each era visible in its stonework — Romanesque base, gothic mid-section, ornate late-gothic upper towers, and a fantastical final wing of pure spires added last and tallest. Curtain-walls link all sections in a long horizontal sweep. The eastern wing cantilevered impossibly over a ravine on massive stone arches, defying gravity with architectural bravado. [A]

A colossal Addams-Family-energy Victorian haunted house fills its lot edge to edge, its facade a controlled chaos of applied ornament — gingerbread trim, gothic pointed arches over every window, a triple-stack of gables climbing the center. Two full-width porches, upper and lower, their railings elaborately turned and partially collapsed. Three turrets of different heights crown the roofline at left, right, and center-right. Every surface is dark with age. [B]

A gothic abbey-fortress in magnificent ruin stretches along a clifftop, its transept walls still soaring to full height, the great east window a tracery skeleton filled with open sky. The ruined cloister walk survives on three sides, its pointed arches draped in ivy. Two massive crossing-towers still stand to different heights, one intact with its stone spire, one broken off mid-shaft and raw. Glorious, enormous, and devastatingly beautiful in its wreckage. [C]

A dark fairytale castle of jaw-dropping asymmetry sprawls in three interconnected masses — a wide low great-hall, a clustered mid-section of six towers all different heights and profiles, and a final high keep that rises in stacked octagonal tiers to a slender crown. Covered arched bridges leap between all three masses at different elevations. Every tower surface is carved with blind tracery. The whole pile reads as one wild, beautiful accident. [D]

A gothic clifftop fortress projects from a sea-stack, connected to mainland by a single great stone bridge of five arches. The castle fans outward from its bridge-gate in a wedge-shape, towers thickening at each corner, the seaward face curving in a great round bastion studded with pointed window-slits. Higher walls rise behind in two more tiers, each receding slightly. The whole structure reads as if the cliff itself grew gothic architecture. [E]

A sprawling gothic manor-estate of deep decayed grandeur spreads wide across its grounds, the main block flanked by two long service wings that turn the composition into a shallow U. Ornate stone quoins frame every corner. The roofline is a spectacular skyline of clustered chimney-stacks, flat-topped parapets, steep gables, and two round towers with conical slate caps. Every window is hooded with a carved drip-mold. Vines reclaim the east wing entirely. [F]

A witch's tower-house of unsettling organic beauty twists upward in seven stacked floors, each story slightly rotated from the one below so the whole structure spirals as it climbs. Gothic windows of varying sizes punctuate the facade without symmetry. A great arched porch at base level, its keystone carved into a screaming face. The roof is a steep conical cap of dark slate with a single iron finial, bent. [G]

A great gothic clocktower cathedral reads as one continuous vertical spectacle — the broad clock-face at mid-height flanked by two projecting stair-turrets, above it a stage of open gothic arcading, then a belfry stage with louvered lancets, then a stone spire with crocketed ribs. The nave extends back behind, its buttresses clear against open sky, gargoyle waterspouts projecting from every clerestory. The whole ensemble is theatrical, ornate, and magnificently severe. [H]

A plantation-gothic ruin of heartbreaking beauty stands at the end of a long avenue of ancient live oaks, its grand colonnade still intact — twelve fluted columns supporting a wide classical pediment now carved through with gothic lancet windows inserted by a later eccentric owner. Behind the portico the house rises in three stories of pointed-arch dormers. Every column is wrapped in wisteria and old vine. The whole facade glows pale as bone. [I]

A frost-palace of white and silver gothic architecture erupts from a glacial plateau in a wide cluster of spires, the central mass low and sprawling, flanked by two immense crystalline towers that rise at different heights. The entire surface is carved in gothic tracery of ice-pale stone, every pointed arch outlined in dark iron. Covered colonnades of slender gothic arches extend from each flank, curving outward like welcoming and threatening arms simultaneously. [J]

A Castlevania-scale ancestral fortress crowns a twin-peaked crag, its curtain-wall running between the two peaks and linking them into one vast fortified complex. On the left peak a great square keep with four corner-towers. On the right peak a cluster of five spires of different heights rising from a round bastion. Between them the curtain-wall bristles with smaller towers, gatehouses, and a central gatehouse bigger than most castles entire. [A]

A Hill-House-energy Victorian manor of suffocating grandeur sprawls behind its iron fence, the main facade a masterwork of oppressive symmetry broken by one wrong window — one extra gable, slightly off-center, that makes the whole composition feel watched. A wraparound porch with turned columns runs the full width. Above: three floors of hooded windows. Above that: a widow's-walk of twisted iron. Above that: a belvedere. The house goes up and up, refusing to end. [B]

A cathedral-abbey fortress complex in spectacular ruin occupies an entire valley head, its nave walls still standing to fifty feet, every clerestory window a stone lacework frame holding open sky. The western towers stand at wildly different heights — one fully intact, one sheared to half-height. A Chapter House dome on the south side has partially collapsed, its ribs spreading outward like a broken crown. Ivy blankets the north transept completely. [C]

A Howl's-Moving-Castle-complexity dark fantasy fortress defies comprehension — an original medieval keep at its core, encrusted with later additions in all directions: cantilevered flying wings braced by gothic arches over empty space, a great hall grafted to the south face with enormous tracery windows, three spires of different eras rising from different sections, and a bridge-tower crossing a gorge to a free-standing gatehouse. Every surface carved. Every addition seemingly impossible. [D]

A Minas-Morgul-dark obsidian palace spreads in a wide crescent, its outer face a sheer curtain of black stone carved with gothic blind-arcading from base to parapet. Seven thin spires of different heights rise from the crescent's curve, all black, all slightly different in profile — some faceted, some round, one twisted. A great gatehouse occupies the crescent's center, its arch tall enough to swallow cathedrals. The whole palace glitters coldly in darkness. [J]

A southern plantation gothic manor crouches beneath an avenue of colossal oaks whose branches have long since engulfed the colonnaded portico. Six massive Doric columns are wrapped to their capitals in Spanish moss and wisteria gone woody and dense as rope. The upper gallery has collapsed on the right side, leaving a dramatic broken edge. Dormers emerge from a steeply pitched tin roof gone completely rust-orange, and iron railings trace the widow's-walk above.

A palace of pure obsidian gothic architecture rising in four stepped tiers, each tier's parapet carved with repeating pointed arches that gleam like cut jet. The black stone catches light in hard-edged facets. Slender needle-spires at every corner cluster in groups of three, and between the first and second tier a covered arcade of pointed arches forms a deep shadow-gallery that wraps the entire structure. The gatehouse towers are enormous, faceted, and brutally beautiful.

A great multi-wing ancestral castle of pale limestone crowns a forested highland ridge, its central keep massive and square, ringed by a tight forest of eight round towers all of different heights. From the keep's crown a sweeping external staircase descends two full stories in a grand curved arc to the inner ward below. Long curtain-walls extend from both flanks and terminate in half-moon bastions bristling with decorative battlements of pointed merlons.

A decayed Victorian haunted mansion of extraordinary width: two full stories of wraparound verandah wrap three sides, the columns ornately carved but half-rotted, some replaced with rough timber props. Four turrets mark the corners — none matching — and a fifth erupts from the center-rear in an octagonal mass topped with a rusted iron finial. The entire east wing has gone dark behind a collapse of the upper floor, every window empty as a socket.

A frost-gothic palace built from translucent pale blue stone that appears lit from within, its impossible spires clustering into a central mass of forty or more needle-thin shafts of graduating heights. Flying buttresses of the same pale material arc between them like frozen jets of water. Every surface is carved in dense repeat-pattern tracery of interlocking pointed arches and snowflake rosettes. The gatehouse is a vault of pure crystalline gothic ribs meeting at a single soaring point.

A cliffside gothic fortress erupts directly from a sea-stack of dark volcanic rock, its foundations indistinguishable from the natural stone. Three massive towers at different heights are connected by two enclosed arched bridges spanning the gaps between rock columns, their windows cracked and dark. The lowest level of wall disappears behind spray-mist even on calm nights. A great iron chain runs from the highest tower down the cliff face to a sea-gate below.

A fairytale-dark fantasy palace of absurd architectural complexity: its roofline is a chaos of steeply-pitched copper gables, miniature spirelets, dormers with their own tiny pointed roofs, and three full-size towers whose tops have been replaced with glass conservatories now shattered and skeletal. A stone skywalk bridges two towers at the third-floor level, its decorative balustrade still intact. The whole thing spreads horizontally in an extravagant silhouette of jagged, theatrical peaks and valleys.

A gothic abbey-castle ruin of heartbreaking grandeur: the great tower still stands to full height, its crown intact and detailed, four corner turrets with their pointed caps perfect against the void. Below, the abbey church has shed its roof and three of its walls, leaving only the skeleton of gothic arcading — pier after elegant pier marching into open air, their stone pale and precise, draped in curtains of dark ivy like mourning vestments.

A grand Southern gothic manor of three full stories plus attic dormers, its façade a controlled riot of cast-iron grillework balconies on every level, the ironwork patterns different on each floor — acanthus, then honeysuckle, then thorned vine. Eight massive brick chimneys rise from the hip roof. The front steps are cracked marble, grass growing in every joint. Massive magnolias press their dark crowns against the upper balcony railings on both sides.

A sprawling gothic manor-estate in the Crimson Peak tradition, its sandstone facade stained deep rust-red by iron-rich soil seeping up through the foundations. The roofline is extravagant: turrets, false gables, multiple chimney stacks in clusters of twos and threes, and a central hall-block rising higher than its flanking wings. Every window is floor-to-ceiling, the upper ones arched, the lower ones topped with Gothic hood-moldings. The whole left wing leans perceptibly outward.

A crooked gothic tower-house of four stacked stories, each floor corbelled outward further than the last so the top story dramatically overhangs the ground by six feet in every direction. The half-timbered uppermost story is pure storybook — steep pointed gable, a round leaded-glass window like an eye, wrought-iron bracket holding a dead lantern. A crumbling stone stair spirals around the exterior, its handrail long gone, its steps mossy and uneven.

A vast Castlevania-scale gothic castle spreads across its mountain in three distinct masses connected by covered walkways and arched bridges at wildly varying heights. The left mass is a cathedral-fronted keep with enormous rose window. The center is the oldest — rougher stone, round towers, minimal ornament. The right mass is the most elaborate: clustered pinnacles, enormous pointed windows, a cantilevered observation platform jutting over the void on two great stone arms.

A gothic clocktower fortress of immense civic-military hybrid character: the clock-face, eight meters across, occupies the entire gable of a massive belltower flanked by two round bastion-towers. Below, the fortified gatehouse is layered in carved decorative stonework — crockets, finials, grotesque faces at every corbel. The arched entrance tunnel is deep enough to swallow carriages whole, its vaulted ceiling carved with a dense foliate pattern. The whole complex is wide, low-slung, and deeply menacing.

A Victorian haunted mansion of Addams Family theatrical maximalism: every gable end sports carved wooden bargeboards in dense gothic tracery patterns, painted black over original white long since peeled to grey. The porch columns are twisted barley-sugar forms. A third-floor balcony wraps the entire front, its railing a repeating pattern of inverted-heart gothic cutouts. Four turrets of varying sizes give the roofline a jagged, exuberant silhouette — wild, decorative, magnificent in its decay.

An ice-gothic palace of black and silver construction: the walls are enormous blocks of obsidian faced with carved silver-grey tracery panels in geometric gothic patterns, the whole surface shimmering with embedded mica. The palace spreads wide in a horseshoe plan, the two wings terminating in massive square towers with elaborately corbelled parapets. Between the towers, a great curtain-wall pierced by a triple-arched gatehouse carries a broad gallery-walk at its crest, carved into pointed arcading all along its length.

A ruined gothic fortress-abbey of extraordinary romantic complexity: five round towers of different diameters stand at irregular intervals, connected by sections of curtain-wall in varying states of survival — some full-height, some reduced to foundations. The great hall block between towers two and three has lost its upper story but retained its entire ground floor, its interior open to the sky and filled with elder saplings pushing through the stone flags. Every surviving surface is sharply detailed.

A fairytale-dark fantasy palace that defies rational engineering: its central mass is a vertical stack of five full gothic stories, each with a full-perimeter arcade of pointed arches, growing narrower as they ascend. From this core, four major wings explode outward at forty-five-degree angles, each wing two stories tall, their rooflines a riot of steeply-pitched copper-green gables, clustered chimneys, and small attendant towers. Flying bridges connect the wing-tips to each other above the courtyards below.

[A] A vast ancestral fortress erupts from a sheer granite crag — five towers of wildly unequal height bristle above curtain walls thick as cliffs, connected by covered battlements and a soaring central keep flanked by octagonal stair-turrets. Flying buttresses arc between wings like stone ribs. Iron portcullises and lancet-windowed galleries stack tier upon tier up the rockface, the whole mass spreading wide across the ridge in brooding, asymmetric grandeur.

[B] A grand Victorian haunted mansion stretches across a weedy promontory — three mismatched turrets of different heights anchor each wing, wrapped in a sagging wraparound porch whose carved railings droop like wilted lace. Broken shutters hang at angles from tall narrow windows. A widow's walk crowns the central gable, its iron railing bent and rusted. Ornate fishscale shingles peel in fans from every steep roofline, giving the whole facade an Addams-family magnificence.

[C] A ruined gothic abbey-castle sprawls in magnificent collapse — the great cathedral nave has lost its roof but retains every soaring pointed arch, ivy threading the tracery like green veins. Crumbling choir towers still stand at each transept corner, their pinnacles broken to jagged crowns. Flying buttresses lean outward at drunken angles, smothered in moss. The gatehouse keeps its portcullis and twin turrets, half-swallowed by creeper, glorious in its gorgeous ruin.

[D] A fairytale-gothic fantasy castle of impossible geometry erupts in every direction at once — clusters of needle-thin spires of five different heights stab the air while a great bulbous onion-domed tower squats beside a soaring rectangular keep. Cantilevered galleries jut out over nothing, supported by lacework stone brackets. Covered skywalks connect mismatched towers at three different levels. The roofline is a jagged fever-dream of dark slate, copper verdigris, and gilded finials gone black.

[E] A gothic sea-fortress clings to a jagged basalt sea-stack, its foundations indistinguishable from the rock itself — spray-blackened towers rise in staggered steps from the waterline, each level a new tier of battlements and arched windows. A great gate-arch spans a sea-chasm, connecting the main keep to a smaller watchtower on the adjacent pinnacle by a daring stone bridge. Salt-eaten tracery still clings to every lancet window, barnacled and magnificent.

[F] Allerdale-Hall-sprawling across a subsiding moor — an enormous gothic manor of rust-red brick and dark timber, four interconnected wings spread in an uneven cruciform. Ornate brick chimneys of twisted barley-sugar columns crowd every roofline. The east wing leans visibly, its foundations swallowed by soft earth. Steep gabled dormers, elaborate corbelled cornices, and a porte-cochere with crumbling carved columns give the whole decayed edifice a heartbreaking, sinking grandeur.

[G] A crooked witch's tower-house leans at an impossible angle over a cliff ledge — three stacked stories of spindly gothic stonework, each floor slightly more warped than the last, crowned by a sharply pointed roof that tilts sideways like a witch's hat. Casement windows glow from within, their diamond panes cracked. Carved grotesques grip every corner. A rickety wooden addition clings to the side, festooned with weather-vanes and dead wind-chimes, utterly, storybook-eerily perfect.

[H] A gothic clocktower-cathedral hybrid dominates a hilltop — an immense rose window faces forward beneath a massive clock-face whose hands have stopped at the wrong hour. Flanking belltowers of unequal height rise above the nave, their belfries ringed by gargoyle balustrades. Steeply arched flying buttresses radiate from the crossing tower on all sides. The entire facade is encrusted with carved foliage, demon-faces, and crocketed pinnacles climbing every available surface.

[I] A crumbling Southern plantation mansion wreathed in spanish-moss spreads wide along a collapsed avenue of live oaks — double-decker colonnaded galleries wrap all four sides, their tall Corinthian columns wound with climbing vine and kudzu. The central pediment has cracked, one pilaster sheared away. Broken shutters frame every tall window. A cupola sits atop the third story, its iron railing collapsed on one side, the whole stately ruin sinking magnificently into subtropical decay.

[J] An obsidian gothic palace of impossible spires rises from a frozen plateau — every surface is black volcanic glass cut into gothic lancets, tracery, and ribbed vaulting visible even on the exterior buttresses. Six spires of graduated height cluster around a great central tower, all faceted like dark crystals. Arched colonnades connect each spire at mid-height, their balustrades carved from the same black stone. The whole structure glitters with cold internal light trapped inside the glass.

[A] A multi-spire mountain fortress spreads across a full ridgeline — a massive rectangular great hall anchors the center while round towers erupt at every corner and interval, each topped with a conical slate roof of different height. Curtain walls drop in stairstepped tiers down both sides of the crag, studded with arrow-loops. A barbican gatehouse projects forward with its own pair of drum towers. The entire complex reads as one long, sprawling, battle-scarred silhouette of concentrated gothic power.

[B] A sprawling Gilded-Age haunted mansion of dark painted wood and gingerbread excess — five distinct gabled peaks of mismatched height run across the facade, each smothered in ornate vergeboards carved with vines and skulls. Wraparound porches curve around both visible corners, their spindles mostly intact, one section sagging. A circular tower with a conical roof anchors the left wing. Tall paired chimneys sprout from every roof section. Every surface is layered, excessive, and glorious.

[C] An abbey-castle in magnificent partial ruin — the great chapter-house walls still stand to full height, their elaborate blind arcading intact, moss mapping every joint. The gatehouse towers retain their full height and corbelled parapets. But the central range has collapsed inward, leaving a cathedral skeleton of pointed arches open to the air, ivy-wrapped and beautiful. A squat defensive keep behind it is entirely intact, brooding over the gorgeous wreckage of everything in front.

[D] A Neuschwanstein-gone-dark fantasy palace twists across a forested peak — asymmetric wings splay left and right at different levels, each terminating in towers of radically different character: a round romanesque drum, a pencil-thin gothic needle, a square keep with machicolations. Covered walkways arc between them at dizzy heights. The main gate is a double-turreted barbican of white stone gone grey with age, smothered in carved knotwork, its drawbridge lowered over a dry moat of dead roses.

[E] A cliffside gothic fortress built directly into a sea-cliff face — its lower walls are the cliff itself, sheer and black, while carved gothic elements emerge gradually higher up: lancet windows, then corbelled turrets, then full battlements and corner towers projecting over the void. A great arched sea-gate at water level opens into darkness. The highest tower is connected to a sea-stack by a single dramatic stone arch bridge, weather-beaten but unbroken.

[F] A vast gothic manor-estate of asymmetric wings and forgotten additions — the original jacobean block is barely visible beneath a century of gothic additions: a new tower here, a conservatory of cracked glass there, a chapel annex sprouting its own small buttresses. Ornate chimneys in every style crowd the roofline. A sweeping grand staircase of cracked stone descends the facade to an overgrown forecourt. The whole rambling structure reads as one long, low, magnificent, decaying organism.

[G] A spindly gothic tower-cottage of three precarious leaning stories, built where no building should stand — its foundation is a jumble of mossy boulders, above which thin gothic lancet windows climb in an irregular spiral. Each floor overhangs the one below by an impossible margin, propped by carved wooden brackets shaped like screaming faces. A steeply pitched roof sprouts a crow-stepped gable on one side and a small turret with its own conical cap on the other.

[H] A cathedral-clocktower of immense gothic ambition — the central tower is capped by an octagonal lantern whose sixteen faces each hold a carved saint-niche, now empty. Great flying buttresses of dark stone radiate in all directions from the crossing, each one terminating in a freestanding pinnacle. The clock-face occupies the full west elevation below the tower, its roman numerals in wrought iron. Lower side aisles extend the building wide on both sides, their rooflines a forest of small carved finials.

[I] A gothic-revival plantation house of staggering ruined beauty — four massive square Doric columns support a Gothic-arched portico in jarring, gorgeous combination. Three stories of floor-to-ceiling shuttered windows rise above. The entire facade is draped in muscadine vine and spanish-moss hanging from a collapsed second-floor gallery. A rear dependency wing extends far to the right, its colonnade of smaller columns also smothered in green. The whole estate radiates a lush, melancholy, distinctly Southern haunting.

[J] A frost-palace of dark blue ice and black iron gothic tracery — pointed arches of frozen water form every window opening, their sills edged in elaborate gothic crocketing of crystal. Clustered ice-spires of five different heights rise from a wide base of faceted ice-blocks cut to resemble ashlar masonry. Iron flying buttresses, now sheathed in hoarfrost, connect the spires at their haunches. The main gate is a soaring pointed arch of dark iron, its spandrels filled with frozen black iron lacework.

[A] A crag-top castle of extreme vertical complexity — four round towers of staggered heights cluster around a great rectangular keep, the whole mass stairstepped and buttressed up the rockface. Between the towers, covered wall-walks run at three different levels, their parapet merlons still sharp. A great hall projects from the keep's flank with its own massive chimney-breast and tall traceried windows. Below the main gate, the crag drops sheer for three hundred feet. Everything reads as one magnificent accumulation of gothic military power.

[B] An enormous haunted Victorian pile of extreme ornamental excess — a central three-story block flanks two asymmetric tower wings, the left one a round turret with a witch's-hat roof, the right a square tower with a widow's walk and iron railing. The front porch runs the full width, its gingerbread brackets elaborate as cathedral tracery. Steep cross-gables project above the second floor windows. Tall paired chimneys with ornamental terra-cotta caps punctuate every roofline. The whole facade is a magnificent theater of Victorian anxiety.
